clue.text: Living in Cambridgeshire setter's found objectionable

parts.note: someone living in that county is of the Fens, the flat drained marshland of eastern England
the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is short for I have, written I'VE

explanation.surface: A Cambridgeshire resident has found something the setter wrote objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the low-lying former marshes of Cambridgeshire; 'found' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensive causes offence, so it is objectionable to the hearer.

clue.text: Core move fails to beat

indicators.note: fails suggests going wrong, so the letters break down and rearrange

explanation.surface: A central manoeuvre falls short in an attempt to win.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to defeat, beat or conquer them.

clue.text: Dugout fenced with iron? Humbug!

indicators.note: fenced with means surrounded, so the iron symbol encloses the rest

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
read as dug out: the word dug knocked out of its order

explanation.surface: A trench shelter surrounded by iron railings; nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dugout' looks like a trench shelter, but read as 'dug out' it asks for DUG jumbled, here UDG, which iron then encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge as an exclamation means nonsense, much like the exclamation humbug.

clue.text: Presently having a job between Scylla and Charybdis

parts.note: presently means now, at this moment
in a situation means in employment, having a post

explanation.surface: Currently employed, but caught between two terrible dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: Scylla and Charybdis were the two sea monsters in Greek myth that ships had to pass between: any course risked disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing two equally bad options, as sailors did passing those monsters, is a predicament with no good outcome.

clue.text: I say! See a diver coming up — it's in cold water

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: say signals that see is heard as the letter it sounds like

parts.note: the word see is pronounced like the letter C

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the bird is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the grebe is a diving waterbird

explanation.surface: An exclamation at spotting a bird surfacing in icy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say! See' gives I then C by sound; 'coming up' reverses GREBE to EBERG.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge floating mass of ice, it drifts in freezing polar seas.

clue.text: The line 4 is least likely to cross

definitions.text: The line 4 is least likely to cross

parts.words: The line 4 is least likely to cross
parts.note: points to the imaginary circle round the hottest part of the globe, where floating ice would melt long before arriving

explanation.surface: The boundary an iceberg is unlikely ever to drift over.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is the answer to 4-down, a mass of floating ice, which melts in warm seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circle midway between the poles is the warmest latitude, so ice could hardly reach it.

clue.text: Man perhaps girl endlessly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the trimmed name is read backwards
endlessly means the girl's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Elsie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man keeps being turned down by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ELSIE to ELSI, which 'rejected' turns round. 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is one example of an island.

clue.text: Fighters' outfit inspires

annotationWithheld.why: Fighters' outfit inspires (9): FIT jumbled (out) inside SPIRES, but 'inspires' must give both the container indicator IN and the fodder SPIRES, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Had Timothy's mother no time for UKIP?

definitions.text: Had Timothy's mother no time for UKIP?

parts.words: Had Timothy's mother no time for UKIP?
parts.note: split the biblical name as the European Union abbreviation plus a word for pleasant, a view a Eurosceptic party would hardly share

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a biblical mother disliked a British anti-Europe party.
explanation.walkthrough: In the New Testament, Eunice is Timothy's mother. UKIP was a party campaigning for Britain to leave the European Union; read as EU NICE, her name is a phrase that party had no time for.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul's letters name her as the mother of his companion Timothy.

clue.text: Unusual brainy idea at inclusion of computer base

indicators.note: unusual suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
inclusion means the idea takes in the little word placed beside it

parts.note: a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: An odd clever idea about including a computer base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer base' is base two, the number system computers use; 'Unusual' and 'inclusion' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Computers work in base two, writing numbers with ones and zeros only.

clue.text: Present design of endless wonder

indicators.note: a design of something is an arrangement of it, so the letters are laid out anew
endless means the word wonder loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A gift whose design is a never-ending marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims WONDER to WONDE, and 'design of' rearranges those letters. 'Present' is a verb here, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone is to present them with a gift or income, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Learning required for issue about sport

indicators.note: about means the issue wraps around the sport

parts.note: an issue of a newspaper or magazine is an edition
RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: Study needed to bring out a publication on sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, the learning a well-read person has acquired.

clue.text: Being in church inclines to purify

indicators.note: being in means the inclines word sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
inclines means leans

explanation.surface: Being part of a church tends to make one cleaner of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make clean, to purify of dirt or sin.

clue.text: Fact, if registered initially, affected commerce

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
initially means only the first letter of registered is used

explanation.surface: Registered facts can influence business dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: FACT, IF and R (from 'registered initially') are rearranged by 'affected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as trade: to traffic in goods is to deal in them commercially.

clue.text: Early office using wireless communication?

parts.note: a playful view of talking to God as a broadcast sent without wires early in the day

explanation.surface: An early job in an office that relies on radio messages.
explanation.walkthrough: An office is also a church service; prayer is pictured as wireless communication with heaven, at the start of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins, the Anglican service said in the morning, is an early office of the church.

clue.text: Dog left me

parts.note: red describes the political left
the setter means himself, the crossword compiler

explanation.surface: A dog walked away from its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb but is the political left; 'me' is the person who wrote the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish breed with a chestnut coat is a gundog.

clue.text: Put off for a rascal

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: Deferred because of a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue parliament is to discontinue its session, putting it off without dissolving it.

clue.text: Cheat makes ringer angrier

parts.note: a ringer is a lookalike, a double
crosser means more annoyed, angrier

explanation.surface: A cheat makes a bell-ringer even more annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringer' suggests a bell-ringer, but here it is a person who looks just like another.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor who betrays a partner while pretending loyalty is a swindler or cheat.

clue.text: Dish to droop in the way

indicators.note: in means the droop word sits inside the way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: A dish that sinks in the middle of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pasta baked with sauce, it is an Italian dish.

clue.text: No firm can stand in reduction from milk producer

indicators.note: in means the reversed pieces go inside the reduction word

parts.note: a cut is a reduction

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: No company can tolerate a cutback from its dairy supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can stand' turns NO + CO upright to OCON, which goes 'in' CUT. Coconuts hold coconut milk.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm fruit contains a milky liquid, so it produces coconut milk.

clue.text: Odd bit turned to cuff

indicators.note: turned means the letters are spun around into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange piece of fabric was folded over to make a cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover piece cut from a larger whole is a stray odd bit.

clue.text: Sit safe around in saloons

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: People sit safely around in bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloons' looks like bars but means cars: the Ford Fiesta is a model of car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiesta is a well-known small Ford car model, so these are named saloon cars.

clue.text: Talk about a mad character

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
the Mad Hatter is a character in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A conversation about an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is idle talk, rapid informal conversation.

clue.text: Sound of cat in Russian forest

indicators.note: sound of means the answer is pronounced like the big cat

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A big cat's call echoes through a Russian woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast coniferous woodland of Siberia is the northern forest belt.

clue.text: Old golfer finds trap in fabric plant

parts.note: Henry Cotton was a British golfer who won the Open three times
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: A veteran golfer discovers a bunker within a fabric factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' means machinery here, not a factory or a growing thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that separates seeds from raw fibre, it is industrial plant for the textile trade.

clue.text: Opposite of noticing what's on confection?

indicators.note: noticing split as not plus a word; its opposite drops the not

explanation.surface: Asks what is the reverse of being aware of a sweet's topping.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'noticing' as NOT + the rest; its opposite simply drops the NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar coating spread on cakes and sweets is what sits on top of a confection.

clue.text: Weary with complete lack of space

indicators.note: lack of means the space is taken away

parts.note: complete means entire
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Tired out with nowhere at all to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of space, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To tire is to grow weary or to make someone weary.

clue.text: Play down posh tea served at former residence of PM

parts.note: ex means former
Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's home
U means upper class, posh

indicators.note: served suggests the tea being dished out, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Downplaying a smart tea that was served at an old prime minister's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' turns TEA into ATE; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To extenuate an offence is to lessen its seriousness, to play it down.
